investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100) — All Remote-Agent Checks Blocked
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". No new agents can be provisioned in the production environment, causing the entire remote-agent feature eval to fail at the creation step before any VM readiness or lifecycle assertions can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard cap of 100 agents per org (or globally, scope unclear from evidence). At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T11:51:28Z), that limit was already at or above 100, causing POST /api/agents to return 409 with "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because all three sibling checks depend on successfully creating an agent via the same POST /api/agents endpoint, all fail with the identical error before any VM ID or remote state can be collected, leaving the expected-output contract entirely unverifiable.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null} at 2026-06-14T11:51:28.273Z–11:51:29.383Z (latency 1110ms).
Sibling check remote-agent-state failed with the identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T11:51:30.234Z (latency 851ms).
Sibling check remote-agent-runtime failed with the identical 409 message at 2026-06-14T11:51:31.084Z (latency 850ms).
All three checks share the same error payload verbatim, confirming the failure is at the shared agent-creation step, not in downstream VM or runtime logic.

Evidence object is empty ({}) for all three checks, confirming no agent was created and no vmId or remoteState was ever collected — the expected-output contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running,idle,ready]) could not be evaluated at all.
The swarm error message embeds a nested JSON error with code=conflict and an explicit numeric limit: 'limit is 100', indicating a hard-coded or configured quota boundary has been reached.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm environment has accumulated 100 or more active/non-cleaned-up agents — either from prior eval runs that were not torn down, from real user agents, or from a combination — and the quota ceiling has been reached.

[Likely secondary] The AURA eval harness creates agents for each check run but does not reliably delete them afterward (e.g., on prior failures or crashes), causing leaked eval agents to accumulate against the quota over time.

[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is scoped to the eval's org/account rather than the entire swarm cluster, meaning the eval org specifically has exhausted its allocation while other orgs may be unaffected.

[Less likely] A swarm-side bug or misconfiguration caused the agent count to be reported as at-limit even if fewer than 100 real agents exist (e.g., a counter desync or a failed delete not decrementing the count).
[Least likely] A deliberate quota reduction was applied to the eval org or the swarm cluster without a corresponding cleanup of existing agents.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exhausted (HTTP 409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T11:51:29–31Z with identical HTTP 409 Conflict responses. The swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation because the agent quota limit of 100 has been reached, preventing the eval harness from provisioning a test agent and causing all downstream state and runtime checks to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The eval harness attempts to provision a new remote agent via POST /api/agents as the first step of each check. The swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", indicating the org-level (or global) agent quota is fully consumed. Because agent creation fails, no agentId is returned, and the subsequent state-polling and runtime-readiness checks cannot proceed — they fail with the same 409 error. This is an eval-layer failure caused by quota exhaustion in the target environment; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1110ms), remote-agent-state (latency 851ms), and remote-agent-runtime (latency 850ms), all ending within a 2-second window at 2026-06-14T11:51:29–31Z.

The 409 response body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.

All three checks have empty evidence objects, confirming no agentId, orgId, readyState, or state was ever returned — matching the expected-output contract's required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) being entirely absent.

Latency for all three failing requests is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (5000ms) and outageLatencyMs threshold (20000ms), indicating the 409 is returned immediately by the swarm backend — not a timeout or network issue.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 agents (the hard quota limit) from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new agent provisioning.
[High confidence] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown/cleanup after each run, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is exhausted.
[Medium confidence] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup step, leaving one or more orphaned agents that pushed the count to the limit.

[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval harness and other workloads (e.g., staging or other automated tests) running against the same org or swarm namespace, and combined usage has reached the ceiling.
[Low confidence] The quota limit itself was recently lowered by a configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.

investigation.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T11:51Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment's org cannot provision a new agent, so no check can progress past the creation step, causing a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature check suite.
investigation.rootCause: The eval harness attempts to create a new swarm agent via POST /api/agents at the start of each check run. The target org in the production eval environment has hit the hard agent quota limit of 100. The swarm backend returns HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before any agent is provisioned. Because all three sibling checks depend on a successful agent creation as their first step, all fail with the same error. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue, not a general product outage — the POST /api/agents endpoint itself is reachable and returning structured errors correctly.
proof: All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the org-level quota cap has been reached.

Latencies for all three checks are well within the warning threshold (850ms, 851ms, 1110ms vs. 20000ms warning / 60000ms outage thresholds), indicating the endpoint is healthy and responding promptly — the failure is a business-logic rejection, not a timeout or infrastructure fault.

The failures are sequential and cascading: remote-agent-create failed at 11:51:29Z, remote-agent-state at 11:51:30Z, and remote-agent-runtime at 11:51:31Z — consistent with a shared dependency on agent creation that was blocked at the first step.
No evidence of broader service degradation: the check config marks this check as required=false, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness org account has accumulated 100 swarm agents from prior eval runs and no cleanup/teardown step is deleting them after each run, exhausting the quota.
[Likely] The eval harness does not assert pre-condition (available agent quota > 0) before attempting creation, so quota exhaustion causes a hard failure rather than a graceful skip or alert.
[Possible] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/cleanup phase, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Less likely] The org-level quota of 100 is too low for the volume of eval runs being executed in this environment and needs to be raised for the eval org.
[Unlikely] A separate workload (non-eval) in the same org is consuming agent quota, crowding out the eval harness.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image generation stream eval failed immediately after `generation_start` because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame and never producing the required `generation_completed` frame or an artifact URL. The harness is either not deployed, misconfigured, or running an incompatible version at the target URL.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The stream received an HTTP 404 when attempting to open a session, which caused an immediate `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame. No progress frames, completion frames, or artifact URLs were ever emitted. This is an eval-environment infrastructure or configuration failure — there is no evidence of impact to production user traffic in the supplied signals.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence contains only two meaningful frames — `generation_start` and `generation_error` — followed by an empty `message` frame; no `generation_completed` frame was ever emitted.
Both required evidence keys (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) are reported missing by the check harness.
The assertion `frameTypes contains generation_completed` and `imageUrlPresent equals true` both failed, consistent with the stream terminating at the error frame.
Total latency was 1940 ms, well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms, confirming the failure was an immediate hard error rather than a timeout.
possibleCauses: (Most likely) The harness process is not running or was never deployed to the URL referenced by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL in the eval environment, causing every session-open request to return 404.
(Likely) The harness is deployed but at a different path or port than what is configured — a URL misconfiguration (trailing slash, wrong base path, wrong port) would produce the same 404.
(Possible) The harness version deployed is incompatible with the eval client's expected API contract — the endpoint route may have been renamed or removed in a newer or older harness build.
(Less likely) A reverse proxy, load balancer, or service mesh in the eval environment is intercepting the request and returning 404 before it reaches the harness process.

Because agent creation fails, no agentId is returned, and the subsequent state-polling and runtime-readiness checks cannot proceed — they fail with the same 409 error. This is an eval-layer failure caused by quota exhaustion in the target environment; no evidence of user-traffic or production incident signals is present in the supplied data.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1110ms), remote-agent-state (latency 851ms), and remote-agent-runtime (latency 850ms), all ending within a 2-second window at 2026-06-14T11:51:29–31Z.

The 409 response body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the quota ceiling has been reached.

All three checks have empty evidence objects, confirming no agentId, orgId, readyState, or state was ever returned — matching the expected-output contract's required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) being entirely absent.

Latency for all three failing requests is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (5000ms) and outageLatencyMs threshold (20000ms), indicating the 409 is returned immediately by the swarm backend — not a timeout or network issue.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] The eval environment's swarm org has accumulated 100 agents (the hard quota limit) from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new agent provisioning.
[High confidence] The eval harness does not perform agent teardown/cleanup after each run, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota is exhausted.
[Medium confidence] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its cleanup step, leaving one or more orphaned agents that pushed the count to the limit.

[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 is shared between the eval harness and other workloads (e.g., staging or other automated tests) running against the same org or swarm namespace, and combined usage has reached the ceiling.
[Low confidence] The quota limit itself was recently lowered by a configuration change, causing previously-passing runs to now fail.

investigations.title: Remote Agents Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) on POST /api/agents
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T11:51Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval environment's org cannot provision a new agent, so no check can progress past the creation step, causing a cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature check suite.
investigations.rootCause: The eval harness attempts to create a new swarm agent via POST /api/agents at the start of each check run. The target org in the production eval environment has hit the hard agent quota limit of 100. The swarm backend returns HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" before any agent is provisioned. Because all three sibling checks depend on a successful agent creation as their first step, all fail with the same error. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue, not a general product outage — the POST /api/agents endpoint itself is reachable and returning structured errors correctly.
proof: All three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) returned HTTP 409 with identical error body: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming the org-level quota cap has been reached.

Latencies for all three checks are well within the warning threshold (850ms, 851ms, 1110ms vs. 20000ms warning / 60000ms outage thresholds), indicating the endpoint is healthy and responding promptly — the failure is a business-logic rejection, not a timeout or infrastructure fault.

The failures are sequential and cascading: remote-agent-create failed at 11:51:29Z, remote-agent-state at 11:51:30Z, and remote-agent-runtime at 11:51:31Z — consistent with a shared dependency on agent creation that was blocked at the first step.
No evidence of broader service degradation: the check config marks this check as required=false, and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness org account has accumulated 100 swarm agents from prior eval runs and no cleanup/teardown step is deleting them after each run, exhausting the quota.
[Likely] The eval harness does not assert pre-condition (available agent quota > 0) before attempting creation, so quota exhaustion causes a hard failure rather than a graceful skip or alert.
[Possible] A previous eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/cleanup phase, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Less likely] The org-level quota of 100 is too low for the volume of eval runs being executed in this environment and needs to be raised for the eval org.
[Unlikely] A separate workload (non-eval) in the same org is consuming agent quota, crowding out the eval harness.
